Hi Alice / Sofia,

Attached is the first drop of artifacts. I ran an internal redaction pass to remove employee-only contact columns and internal ticket IDs. High-level notes below; please see attachments for detailed answers.

Key points:
- Persistence: Redwood’s hosted inference runtime does not persist customer prompt text to durable storage. KV cache is ephemeral (TTL configurable, default 6 hours) and is used for in-flight session performance only. Cached values are evicted automatically; we do not index or retain prompt text in logs beyond aggregated monitoring (sampling only for telemetry).
- SOC 2 in-scope: Serving runtime, control plane (authn/authz for API keys), observability pipeline (retention/aggregation). Excluded: customer-hosted private deployments where the customer manages storage and keys. We included a one-pager SOC2-summary_20270420.pdf.
- KMS & residency: We operate multi-region KMS with customer-key scoping. Subprocessors with EU residency are marked in the roster (see redwood_subprocessor_roster_20270419.csv). For customers requiring EU-only processing, Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem) is available; we can scope deployment/terms separately.
- CAIQ: we included a text file with Drive links to our CAIQ export and artifact IDs.

See attachments: redwood_subprocessor_roster_20270419.csv (CSV), SIG-Lite-answers_20270420.pdf, CAIQ-links_20270420.txt, SOC2-summary_20270420.pdf.

Ben Carter
Senior Security Engineer, Redwood Inference

Hi Alice — answers inline and next steps below.

1) Long-term access to unredacted prompts: No third-party subprocessor has long-term access to unredacted customer prompts for hosted deployments. The KV cache is ephemeral by default (6h TTL) and is not materialized to long-term storage. Third parties that process data (for example, cloud infra providers or telemetry processors) only receive aggregated, sampled telemetry and do not receive raw prompt text. We can provide a tech annex that diagrams the data flow if that helps auditors.

2) KMS / EU residency: For customers selecting EU residency on hosted Redwood, master KMS keys are scoped to EU regions and managed under our KMS tenancy with restricted access controls (see row in roster flagged "EU-KMS: true"). For the strictest residency requirements we recommend Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem); in that model the customer can bring their own key or we can set up a dedicated HSM in-region under an enterprise contract. Ben — I can loop you into a short tech call with Skyline’s cloud/security architects if desired.

3) NDA: Contracts (contracts@redwood.com) is copied here — they can send Skyline a one-off mutual NDA. Irene — legal, can you please confirm the standard 7-day review and any non-negotiable clauses?

Deliverables: I’ve posted the packet to Drive (link below) and added a README that maps artifacts to your procurement checklist. If you’d like a signed attestation from Ben about eviction policies and telemetry sampling, we can provide that on company letterhead.

Drive: https://drive.redwood.com/shared/skyline/transparency-packet-20270420

Thanks — talk soon,
Sofia Ivanova
